39.0.0.en: 1 At that time Merodach-baladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah: for he had heard that he had been sick, and was recovered. 2 And Hezekiah was glad of them, and shewed them the house of his precious things, the silver, and the gold, and the spices, and the precious ointment, and all the house of his armour, and all that was found in his treasures: there was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah shewed them not.

39.0.1.en: Hezekiah’s star rose because of the defeat of Sennacherib king of Assyria, and Hezekiah offered a psalm of thanksgiving to God, especially after God gave him fifteen years more of his life; but he did not practice thanksgiving in his life, for his heart was lifted up and he became haughty (2 Chr 32:26), and he had “exceeding much riches and honour, and he made himself treasuries for silver, and for gold, and for precious stones, and for spices, and for shields, and for all manner of pleasant vessels... and he made himself towers, and possessions of flocks and herds in abundance: for God had given him substance very much” (2 Chr 32:27-29).

39.0.2.en: God left him in the midst of this wealth and glory for a time, and wanted to discover what was in his heart (2 Chr 32:31), so He allowed Merodach-baladan, king of Babylon, to send letters and a present after his healing. It was fitting for Hezekiah to glorify God and to show forth the grace of God, not to reveal his treasures. He fell into self-reliance and the display of his own glory, as Samson had fallen before, who disclosed the secret of his strength to the harlot and so collapsed.

39.0.3.en: “Merodach” is a title borne by many persons; it is the name of the king of the gods, mentioned together with Bel (Jer 50:2), and is symbolized by the planet Mars. His name is often part of the name of one of the kings of Babylon. As for “Baladan,” its meaning is: “a son has been given.”

39.0.4.en: St. Hippolytus says: [Merodach the Chaldean, king of Babylon at that time, was astonished when he studied astronomy and measured these bodies and learned the cause, so he sent a letter and gifts, as the Magi from the East did with Christ.]

39.1.0.en: Hezekiah was carried away by the pride of his heart and his love of vain worldly glory, so as to reveal everything he had to the messengers of Merodach-baladan: “there was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Hezekiah shewed them not” [2]. Hezekiah had not experienced the words of David his father: “The glory of the king’s son is from within” (Ps 45).

39.1.1.en: * Vainglory has the power to blind the minds of those who are captive to it, even to plain truths, and to lead them to dispute even matters that are generally agreed upon...

39.1.2.en: * Those who are enslaved by zeal for the glory of this present world cannot obtain the glory that is from God. For this reason the Lord rebukes them: “How can ye believe, which receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that cometh from the (only) God?” (cf. Jn 5:44).

39.1.3.en: This passion is a kind of intense drunkenness, and whoever submits to it is hard to cure. It separates the souls of its captives from heavenly things and nails them to the earth; it does not let them look to the true light but urges them to wallow in the mud; it sets over them harsh masters who dominate them, needing only to give orders.

39.1.4.en: Whoever is struck by this disease acts according to his own whim...

39.2.s.en: 2. The divine command to take away the treasures:

39.2.0.en: 3 Then came Isaiah the prophet unto king Hezekiah, and said unto him, “What said these men? and from whence came they unto thee?” And Hezekiah said, “They are come from a far country unto me, even from Babylon.” 4 Then said he, “What have they seen in thine house?” And Hezekiah answered, “All that is in mine house have they seen: there is nothing among my treasures that I have not shewed them.” 5 Then said Isaiah to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD of hosts: 6 Behold, the days come, that all that is in thine house, and that which thy fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried to Babylon: nothing shall be left, saith the LORD. 7 And of thy sons that shall issue from thee, which thou shalt beget, shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.”

39.2.1.en: God sent His prophet Isaiah to Hezekiah to discipline him, and he asked him:

39.2.3.en: * And from whence came they unto thee?

39.2.4.en: * What have they seen in thine house?

39.2.5.en: He did not answer the most important question: “What said these men?”

39.2.6.en: He thought that they had come from a far country, from Babylon [3], and so there was no danger to him from them; therefore the divine sentence of punishment was issued through Babylon.

39.3.0.en: The punishment came severe, because pride is an exceedingly dangerous disease, meaning fellowship in the nature of Satan. Hezekiah would not only lose the treasures he had revealed, but would also lose the freedom of his children, who would become eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon [7].

39.3.1.en: Origen holds that pride is the chief sin of Satan. St. John Chrysostom says: [Satan would not have fallen and become Satan had he not been struck by this disease. It cast him out of confidence (in God) and brought him to the pit of fire, and it is the cause of all woes. It is able to destroy every good thing of the soul, whether there is giving (the offering of alms) or prayer or fasting or anything else... Nothing is more foolish than the proud man, even if wealth surrounds him, or he has gained much of the wisdom of this world, or is found in a royal palace...]

39.4.0.en: “Then said Hezekiah to Isaiah, Good is the word of the LORD which thou hast spoken. He said moreover, For there shall be peace and truth in my days.” [8].

39.4.1.en: Outwardly the king uttered words that carry submission, but we do not know what his attitudes and motives were; perhaps it was a surrender without repentance and without trust in God, who is able to forgive sins.

39.4.2.en: He confessed that he had sinned, but he did not offer repentance. The proof of this is that instead of crying out to God with tears in order to return to Him, he felt reassured that the discipline would come after his death, in the days of his children. He carried a kind of selfishness, for he was concerned to spend his days in peace, with no concern for what would befall the people and his descendants afterward.

40.0.s.en: 1. Comfort ye, comfort ye my people:

40.0.0.en: 1 Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God. 2 Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORD’s hand double for all her sins.

40.0.1.en: God was accustomed to ascribe the people to Himself when He was pleased with them, calling them “My people”; but in the case of their disobedience He sometimes ascribes them to Moses (Ex 32:7) or calls them “the people” (Ex 32:9), and more plainly He says, “not my people” (Hos 1:9), in order to provoke them so that they would return to Him, and then He returns to ascribing them to Himself (Hos 2:23). But here, as He opens before them, indeed before believing humanity, the door of salvation, He calls them “My people.”

40.0.2.en: The prophet was accustomed to repeat some words twice, as here, “Comfort ye, comfort ye” (Isa 51:9, 17; 5:1), because he is speaking of the Church of the New Testament that comes from two groups, the Jews and the Gentiles; for it is the Church of love, which unites and binds together, since the number 2 points to love. Love makes the two one.

40.1.0.en: It is the Church of love, by which God binds her to Himself as a bridegroom to his bride, and which binds the members coming from all the nations as one body to the one Head. Through this love He addresses her, saying, “Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem” [2]; the literal translation is “speak to the heart of Jerusalem,” an expression repeated eight times in the Old Testament (Gen 34:3; 50:21; Judg 19:3; Ruth 2:13; 2 Sam 19:7; 2 Chr 20:22; Hos 2:14) and directed to a beloved man or woman. The Church here is the bride of Christ, beloved of Him, and He speaks to her in the language of love, which only the heart understands. It is the language in which He spoke most plainly and profoundly through the Cross, to acquire humanity as His bride (Rev 19:7; 21:2, 9).

40.1.1.en: It is an invitation that the Bridegroom offers to His suffering bride, that in the midst of her sufferings she may look to the joyful end, and so bear suffering in hope and with joy, like her Bridegroom, who suffered for the joy that was set before Him (Heb 12:2), since He saw our salvation and glorification in His bearing of the Cross. As the Apostle says: “For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ” (2 Cor 5:1).

40.1.2.en: What is the secret of our comfort? God says: “I, even I, am he that comforteth you” (Isa 51:14). This is the secret of our comfort: the Father comes forward to receive us to Himself as His children, through our union with Christ, the Only-Begotten Son, who offers His life as an atonement for our sins as the secret of our comfort: “our consolation also aboundeth by Christ” (2 Cor 1:5). Our Christ, who has received us to Himself by His blood, gives us His Holy Spirit, “the Comforter,” who fills our hearts with Him, establishing the kingdom of joy in our hearts. For this reason He gives a speech directed to the heart, saying, “Speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her, that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned: for she hath received of the LORD’s hand double for all her sins” [2].

40.1.3.en: From the literal side, the prophet looks at the captivity that befalls the people not as a political disaster that happened by chance or as the fruit of military weakness, but as a divine permission for the sake of discipline. She received the discipline twofold, for on the one hand she committed sins unbecoming to her, and on the other hand she did not practice the righteousness of God or do good. The divine commandment requires us to cease from evil and to do good.

40.1.4.en: From the prophetic side, as she looks to her crucified Bridegroom she finds that He has paid the debt for her in the fullest form, not merely to relieve her of the debt but to justify her by His blood and sanctify her, so that she enjoys fellowship in His glories. It is as though the supplications of humanity, which David the prophet expressed, had been fulfilled when he said: “Look upon mine affliction and my pain; and forgive all my sins” (Ps 25:18).

40.1.5.en: Now the prophet looks at the procession of the people returning to Jerusalem as a symbol of the procession of those redeemed by the blood of the Lord of glory, Jesus, and St. John the Baptist came to prepare the way for this heavenly Messianic procession.

40.2.s.en: 2. Preparing the way for the Lord:

40.2.0.en: 3 The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, “Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God. 4 Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low: and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain: 5 And the glory of the LORD shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it.” 6 The voice said, “Cry.” And he said, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field: 7 The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: because the spirit of the LORD bloweth upon it: surely the people is grass. 8 The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.”

40.2.1.en: Perhaps the prophet Isaiah heard a heavenly voice calling the heavenly ones to prepare the procession of the return from captivity to Jerusalem. For the prophet Ezekiel had previously seen the glory of the Lord departing from the city (Ezek 11:22-25), and now the procession returns with the return of the captives, as though it were a royal procession led by God Himself, the liberator of His children!

40.2.2.en: But the greater procession is the preparation of the way for the entrance of the Messiah the Savior into the life of humanity, which was accomplished by St. John the Baptist, the angel of the Lord, through preaching repentance and proclaiming the need for a Savior (Mk 1:3; Mt 3:3; Lk 3:4-6; Jn 1:22).

40.3.0.en: St. John was the voice that resounds in the wilderness to prepare the way for the divine Word, proclaiming that every arrogant and haughty soul is brought down [4], and every crooked heart becomes straight, and all obstacles vanish, because the glory of the Lord is revealed through the Messiah the Savior, and all flesh sees it together, both Jews and Gentiles. Therefore the prophet says: “The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God. Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low: and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain: and the glory of the LORD shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it” [3-5].

40.3.1.en: John was called a “voice,” while Christ was called the “Word,” and how great the difference between the voice and the word! For the Fathers say that the voice is what is heard by the ear, while the word is what is grasped by the mind. So John came as a witness to Christ, the divine Word:

40.3.2.en: * Perhaps this explains how Zechariah lost his voice at the birth of the “voice” who points toward the Word of God, and was not healed of this until after the birth of the “voice” who precedes the Word. The voice must be perceived by the ear so that the mind receives the Word toward whom the “voice” points. John points toward Christ, because the speech (the word) is made known by means of the voice.

40.3.3.en: Origen * From our speech you know that the “voice” comes first when the “word” is heard; therefore John declares of himself that he is a “voice,” since he goes before the “Word.” By his coming before the Lord he was called a “voice,” and by his ministry men heard “the word of the Lord.” He cries out, proclaiming: “make his paths straight”... The way of the Lord to the heart is straight when it receives with humility His words of truth; it is straight if we conduct our lives in agreement with His commandments. Therefore it is said: “If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him” (Jn 14:23).

40.3.4.en: Father Gregory the Great * Isaiah was aware of John’s work of evangelism, for while Isaiah calls Christ God and Lord (Isa 9:6), he points to John as a messenger and servant, and a lamp that shines before the appearing of the true Light. He is the morning star that announces the rising of the sun from beyond the horizon, whose brilliant rays then dispel the dense curtains of darkness. John was a voice, not the Word, going before Christ as the voice goes before the word.

40.3.5.en: St. Cyril the Great With what does this voice cry out? With the Gospel of the New Testament, which is the way of the Lord, which lifts the humble souls up to the heavenly life, and breaks down the pride of the haughty; it renews the creation that had become crooked so that it walks uprightly, and removes the obstacles from before it, so that the Lord is glorified in believing humanity [3-5].

40.3.6.en: * May you walk in the royal way, not turning from it to the right or to the left, but may the Spirit lead you through the narrow gate; then all your affairs will prosper when you are examined there in Christ Jesus our Lord.

40.3.7.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus “The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness” [3] resounds in the wilderness of this barren life, since it does not bear within it the tree of life as in the first Paradise; he came to proclaim the Lord Christ, the tree of life, who is planted in the wilderness of our nature to make of it a fruitful Paradise by His dwelling in us. In this sense St. Ambrose says: [Before the Son of God raised up the members of the Church, He began His work in His servant John; for this reason St. Luke (Lk 3:2) informs us that the word of God came at once upon John the son of Zechariah in the wilderness... This was accomplished in the desolate wilderness, for “the children of the desolate are more than the children of her which hath a husband” (Isa 54:1), and it was said to her, “Rejoice, O barren one that didst not bear” (Isa 54:1)... for she had not yet been planted among the foreign peoples... and He had not yet come who said, “But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God” (Ps 52:8), and the heavenly Vinedresser had not yet given fruit to the branches (Jn 15:1). So the voice rang out in order that the wilderness might bring forth fruit.]

40.3.8.en: * Let the way of the Lord be prepared in our heart, for the heart of man is great and wide, as if it were the world. Look at its greatness not in bodily size, but in the power of the mind, which gives it the ability to embrace a very great knowledge of the truth.

40.3.9.en: Therefore let the way of the Lord be prepared in your heart through a worthy life and through good and perfect works, so that this way may keep your life upright, and the words of the Lord may enter you without hindrance.

40.4.0.en: Origen St. Augustine observed that the prophet used the word “flesh” in the phrase “And the glory of the LORD shall be revealed, and all mankind (flesh) shall see it together” [5], and that by this he does not mean the flesh without the soul but the whole man, for Holy Scripture often uses the word “flesh” or “soul” to mean the man. For the one who beholds the glory of the Lord is the whole man [for the flesh alone without the soul sees nothing].

40.4.1.en: When the Evangelist said, “the Word was made flesh” (Jn 1:14), he did not mean that the Word of God took flesh without a human soul, as Apollinaris claimed, which led Pope Athanasius the Apostolic to write a book against his friend Apollinaris, in which he refutes his opinions.

40.5.0.en: The prophet Isaiah heard another heavenly voice affirming that all flesh (man) is like the grass of the earth (Ps 90:5; 103:15), “but the word of our God shall stand for ever” [8]. Whoever clings to the dust of the earth or to the love of temporal things becomes passing grass, and whoever clings to the Lord Christ, “the Word of God,” rises with Him to live in His glory forever. This is the way that Holy Scripture has prepared for receiving the Savior: our commitment to fellowship with the One who transforms us from the passing grass of the earth into fellowship with Him and abiding in Him eternally in His glories. As St. Augustine says: [If a man longs for true rest and true happiness, he must lift his hope above mortal, passing things and fix it on the word of the Lord, so that, clinging to it, it remains forever and he remains with it eternally.]

40.5.1.en: Origen comments on the saying that “all flesh is grass,” saying: [The Lord Christ commanded the multitudes to sit down on the grass (Mt 14:21) in order to feed them, meaning that if a man subdues his body (sitting on the grass) and places all temporal things under the leadership of the soul, so that he walks wholly in the Holy Spirit, then he enjoys the blessings of the Lord Christ and the true satisfaction. We cannot meet our Christ or receive His divine gifts through the disciples, that is, the Church, as long as we live according to the flesh. Therefore let us subject the body to our souls by the Holy Spirit and let us recline on the grass, so that the body may be an obedient servant working in harmony with the soul without resisting it; then we shall enjoy spiritual things.

40.5.2.en: The following are some comments of the Fathers on the phrase “All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field: the grass withereth, the flower fadeth: because the spirit of the LORD bloweth upon it” [6-7].

40.5.3.en: Look, for whatever your soul clings to, it clings to forever. If you cling to the grass and the flower of the grass, you bind your soul to the grass that withers and the flower that falls, and God will destroy these in the end.

40.5.4.en: * Since God, as a Father, knows our formation, that we are nothing but dust that can flourish only for a time, He sent us His Word, and this Word of His remains forever. He made Him a brother to the grass that does not last.

40.5.5.en: Do not marvel, for you have become a partaker with Him in His eternity, since He first shared with you in the grass.

40.5.6.en: * So Moses did with the head of the calf [(Ex 32:20) he burned it with fire], for the head of the calf represents a great mystery, in that it represents the flesh of the wicked, because it eats grass and seeks temporal things; for all flesh is grass...

40.5.7.en: St. Augustine * Why do you fear temporal things that pass like the course of a river?! For this is the nature of present things, whether joyful or painful. Another prophet compares human prosperity to grass.

40.5.8.en: St. John Chrysostom * We hear this and the like every day, and yet we remain nailed to the earth.

40.5.9.en: St. John Chrysostom * I know that some try to show that these words (all flesh is grass) refer to the condition of barbarous people of different nations and different customs, who came to faith (in the word of the Lord) and so came into the harmony of the righteous.

40.6.0.en: 9 O Zion, that bringest good tidings, get thee up into the high mountain; O Jerusalem, that bringest good tidings, lift up thy voice with strength; lift it up, be not afraid; say unto the cities of Judah, “Behold your God! 10 Behold, the Lord GOD will come with strong hand, and his arm shall rule for him: behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him. 11 He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young.” 12 Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance? 13 Who hath directed the Spirit of the LORD, or being his counsellor hath taught him? 14 With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the way of truth, and taught him knowledge, and shewed to him the way of understanding? 15 Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the small dust of the balance: behold, he taketh up the isles as a very little thing. 16 And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering. 17 All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity. 18 To whom then will ye liken God? or what likeness will ye compare unto him? 19 The workman melteth a graven image, and the goldsmith spreadeth it over with gold, and casteth silver chains. 20 He that is so impoverished that he hath no oblation chooseth a tree that will not rot; he seeketh unto him a cunning workman to prepare a graven image, that shall not be moved. 21 Have ye not known? have ye not heard? hath it not been told you from the beginning? have ye not understood from the foundations of the earth? 22 It is he that sitteth upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers; that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in: 23 That bringeth the princes to nothing; he maketh the judges of the earth as vanity. 24 Yea, they shall not be planted; yea, they shall not be sown: yea, their stock shall not take root in the earth: and he shall also blow upon them, and they shall wither, and the whirlwind shall take them away as stubble. 25 “To whom then will ye liken me, or shall I be equal?” saith the Holy One. 26 Lift up your eyes on high, and behold who hath created these things, that bringeth out their host by number: he calleth them all by names by the greatness of his might, for that he is strong in power; not one faileth.

40.6.1.en: Now, after showing that whoever is attached to perishable temporal things becomes like the grass of the earth that withers, while whoever clings to the eternal Word of God remains with Him forever, he declares the meaning of attachment to the word of the Lord.

40.6.2.en: a. Receiving the joyful evangelical message: “O Zion, that bringest good tidings, get thee up into the high mountain; O Jerusalem, that bringest good tidings, lift up thy voice with strength; lift it up, be not afraid; say unto the cities of Judah, Behold your God! Behold, the Lord GOD will come with strong hand, and his arm shall rule for him” [9-10].

40.6.3.en: Who is she that lifts up her voice but the Church of the New Testament, which ascends with humanity as upon the mountain of the Word of God through the preaching of the disciples and the apostles, indeed through the witness of all the people; she ascends with souls to the heavenly life, or the new life that has become ours in Christ Jesus, to meet God our Savior as a source of joy and exultation. She sees Him coming to her to rule in her depths and to establish His kingdom by His lofty arm.

40.6.4.en: b. Perceiving the reality of God; for as we are lifted up to the new life we meet the Lord on a personal level, and we do not find Him a hidden, unknown power but a Being who deals with us: “He comes and rules and rewards and cares, etc... As St. Gregory of Nyssa says in his reply to Eunomius: [Is God, then, an energy and not a person?]

40.6.5.en: St. John Cassian says: [It befits us, when we hear the word “His arm” or the like, not to understand it in a bodily, material sense.

40.7.0.en: c. Discovering God’s care for us, as He is the Shepherd who is concerned for His flock [11], and He is unique in His person as in His care:

40.7.1.en: * He is the almighty Creator in His care: “Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?” He is the Creator of the waters and the heavens, as of the dust and the solid mountains. He who created is able to renew creation.

40.7.2.en: The waters point to the peoples, the heavens to the soul, the earth to the body, and the mountains and hills to man’s abilities and gifts; as if God in His care is almighty, renewing the Church as a whole by joining the peoples to her, and renewing every soul together with the body, with its energies, senses, feelings and capacities.

40.7.3.en: He measures and weighs everything, for He is all-powerful.

40.7.4.en: Perhaps he wanted to affirm that God cares for His lifeless creation, from the waters and the firmament of heaven to the dust and the mountains and hills; so how would He not care for us, who are in His image and likeness, and for whose sake He created the whole world?

40.7.5.en: * If you doubt God’s providence, ask the earth and the heaven and the sun and the moon. Ask the irrational beings and the crops... Ask the rocks and the mountains and the sand dunes and the hills. Ask the night and the day; for God’s providence is clearer than the sun and its rays, in every place: in the wilderness and the cities and the inhabited world, on the earth and in the seas... Wherever you go you hear a speaking testimony to this crying providence.

40.8.0.en: St. John Chrysostom * All-wise: “Who hath directed the Spirit of the LORD, or being his counsellor hath taught him? With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the way of truth, and taught him knowledge, and shewed to him the way of understanding?” [13-14].

40.8.1.en: Though He is the almighty Creator who brought nature into being for our sake and cares for it and looks after it, He is also all-wise, who knows what is for our salvation and edification; His plan is not our plan, and His ordinances are higher than ours (Rom 11:34).

40.8.2.en: * He (the Apostle Paul, Rom 11) did not say only that His judgments are past finding out, but also that they are beyond searching out. Not only can man not understand them, he cannot even begin to search them out. It is impossible for him to grasp their end or even to discover how their planning began.

40.8.3.en: * He wants to say that He is the fountain and source of all good things, and has no need of a partner or counsellor.

40.9.0.en: St. John Chrysostom * The Almighty: nothing escapes His hand: “Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the small dust of the balance: behold, he taketh up the isles as a rudder...” [15].

40.9.1.en: He is the Almighty... So if the nations want to rule the world and dominate it through violence and force, they are exceedingly weak; God sees them as a drop of water in a bucket and the dust of a balance... But God, in the weakness and foolishness of the Cross, rules and reigns with power and authority over the depths.

40.9.2.en: The earth with all its peoples is very small to the Savior; He carries it like dust on a small scale; and the inhabitants of the isles, who boast of their merchant and war ships, all of them together are like a rudder that the Lord holds in His hand!

40.9.3.en: * He (God) comprehends in Himself all rational creation so that all things remain in existence, held together by His power, which embraces all.

40.10.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa * His concern for the nations: “And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering. All nations before him are as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity” [16-17]. A poetic picture of the nations’ acceptance of faith in God, so that all the trees of Lebanon (the cedars) do not suffice to kindle the altar of the Lord and all its beasts do not suffice to offer burnt offerings... The need has become for the wood of the Cross, which towers above all the cedars of Lebanon, and the sacrifice of Christ, which cannot be compared with all the animal sacrifices. Through this altar (the Cross) and this sacrifice the Gentiles enjoy salvation.

40.10.1.en: * The living divine Lamb reached the place of sacrifice, and the crucifiers stood like high priests offering Him as a victim...!

40.10.2.en: * Our Lord was crucified and bore the sins of the world, and nailed sin with nails so that it might not reign. When they crucified Him, He crucified it with Him on Golgotha, lest it kill other generations.

40.10.3.en: Mar Jacob of Serugh * The greatness of the Lord Christ, the Savior and the Sacrifice:

40.11.0.en: “To whom then will ye liken God? or what likeness will ye compare unto him?” [18]; the cost of idols is heavy, requiring gold and silver or wood that will not rot, together with the cost of the cunning workman who makes them [20], and set against this is the thieves’ longing to steal them; but our Christ offers a free salvation, and proclaims His kingdom in the heart, where no one can steal it from our depths.

40.12.0.en: * “He that sitteth upon the sphere of the earth” [22]. The prevailing belief was that the earth is flat and not a sphere, but Isaiah saw the Lord sitting upon the sphere of the earth like a king sitting on his throne, establishing His kingdom in the hearts of men.

40.12.1.en: * “The inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers; that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in” [22]. He does not reign out of need for the service of earthly or heavenly beings, but out of love and fatherly care. The earthly beings are to Him like the grasshopper (locust), and the heaven is like a piece of cloth or a tent. The great ones are as nothing to Him, and the judges, like vanity, dissolve.

40.12.2.en: Earth and heaven are as nothing compared with His power; but in His love He reigns over and leads the earthly and the heavenly as King and Savior..

40.13.0.en: The astrologers were occupied with the calculations of the heavens and their systems, but God knows all their details as their Creator, and calls them by names [26]; so how would He not know every man and care for his salvation?!

40.14.0.en: 27 Why sayest thou, O Jacob, and speakest, O Israel, “My way is hid from the LORD, and my judgment is passed over from my God”? 28 Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard, that the everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary? there is no searching of his understanding. 29 He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength. 30 Even the youths shall faint and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall: 31 But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

40.14.1.en: Those who deny the faith often think that God, in His own realm, is far from the circle of men: He is in His heavens while man lives in his world... This is the essence of contemporary atheistic thought, and it is an ancient thought with which the enemy strikes man in order to make him lose his meeting with his Creator and union with Him and fellowship. As it is stated here in this book: “Why sayest thou, O Jacob, and speakest, O Israel, My way is hid from the LORD, and my judgment is passed over from my God” [27].

40.14.2.en: This is what man repeats in the midst of his spiritual weariness... He counts himself alone, isolated even from God, who does not care about man’s way and his life. Perhaps this is what the captives said, as they thought that God had forgotten them completely; months and years passed as though He had broken His covenant with their fathers and no longer thought of them or cared for their return. He does not care about their cause or concern Himself with their way; He left them in Babylon and remained in His heavens, not moving to remove their disgrace and lift humiliation and bondage from them.

40.14.3.en: The prophet replies to this as follows:

40.15.0.en: a. The continuity of God’s work: God in His love may be patient, but He continues in His care for man, “fainteth not, neither is weary” [28]. He is “the everlasting God,” His love never passes away and His covenant is eternal and unchanging.

40.15.1.en: b. His judgments cannot be searched out [28]... He saves in an unexpected way.

40.16.0.en: c. Because of our sins we grow weak in our faith, but He “giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength” [29]; therefore we need to place the matter in His hands, and He will sustain us even in our faith.

40.17.0.en: d. He gives us His Holy Spirit, who renews our nature and lifts us up on the wings of the Spirit as to heaven itself, and we rise without anxiety... “But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint” [31].

40.17.1.en: * By the Holy Spirit we are freed from slavery and called to freedom!

40.17.2.en: By Him we have become children of God by His adoption of us!

40.17.3.en: And above all this, if I may say so, we have been renewed, putting off from us the hateful weight of sins...!

40.17.4.en: Through Him we receive the forgiveness of sins, and by Him we are cleansed from every stain, and through His gift we are changed from human beings into angels, who share with us in the enjoyment of His grace; yet we do not become so at once, but, what is marvelous, while we are still in human nature we show a conduct in life that befits angels!

40.17.5.en: Such then is the power of the Spirit...
